false_signal_from_concurrent_test_execut.symptom: a second full-suite run (launched to re-validate after the ConsumerReadProductAntiBypassTest fix) reported 51 errors and 15 failures across entirely unrelated MariaDB-backed producer capture suites (B18ProducerCalendarRegistryTest, B18ProducerEventFactorCaptureTest, B18ProducerRawInputLineageTest, B18ProducerTemporalPopulationTest, and others) -- none of which touch AsKnownReplaySnapshotService, MarketDataReadProductService or ReplayResultRepository.
false_signal_from_concurrent_test_execut.cause: the three-probe re-verification (P1/P2/P3, each mutating and restoring the same production files) was run concurrently with that background full-suite process, contending for the same shared MariaDB instance the C1 producer capture tests write to and roll back against -- the same class of race E-050 diagnosed for a full run started before concurrent documentation edits landed.
false_signal_from_concurrent_test_execut.diagnosis: MariaDB error log showed no crash, no restart and no error entries across either run; the server was reachable throughout. This rules out server-side corruption and points to client-side test contention from running multiple PHPUnit processes against the shared instance at once.
false_signal_from_concurrent_test_execut.resolution: production and test file hashes were confirmed unchanged from the corrected, probe-verified state; a third full-suite run was launched with zero concurrent processes (confirmed via process list beforehand and by running nothing else until it completed) and reproduced exactly the known 7-failure baseline, taken as the authoritative result.
false_signal_from_concurrent_test_execut.lesson: never run an additional PHPUnit invocation while a full-suite regression is in flight against the same MariaDB instance, even for file restore verification.
